chapter_name: The Parliamentary System: Legislature and Executive
learning_objective: 🎯 Dive into the heart of India's democracy to learn how laws are made, who runs the country, and how the government works as a team!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Parliament is the supreme law-making body of India. It has three main parts: the President of India, the Lok Sabha (House of the People), and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Together, they debate and decide what is best for the country.

The Legislature is the branch of government responsible for making laws. Members of Parliament (MPs) discuss national issues, ask tough questions, and vote on new rules to keep society running smoothly and fairly.

While the Legislature makes the laws, the Executive puts them into action! This team is led by the Prime Minister and their Council of Ministers. They are responsible for running government departments like health, education, and defense.

main_concepts.concept_title: 📄 How a Bill Becomes a Law
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A 'Bill' is simply a rough draft of a proposed law. To become an actual law, it must be carefully discussed and passed by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. Finally, it goes to the President for their signature. Once signed, it becomes a law!

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ Host a Mini-Parliament!
fun_activity.instructions: Gather your friends or family and propose a new 'House Rule' (like extra playtime). Have a debate where one side argues for the rule and the other against it, then take a vote to see if your 'Bill' passes!

quick_recap: ⭐ India follows a Parliamentary system of government with two main branches: Legislature and Executive.
⭐ The Legislature (Parliament) discusses problems and makes laws for the whole country.
⭐ The Executive (Prime Minister and Ministers) implements these laws and runs the daily administration.
⭐ The Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha.
⭐ A Bill must be passed by both houses and signed by the President to become a formal law.
